claims.text: The as-deposited non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi alloy is in an ordered, single-phase hexagonal state.
Cold rolling followed by mild annealing will refine the alloy's grains.
Cold rolling followed by mild annealing will induce crystallographic texture.
The processing intervention will increase grain-boundary density.
The processing intervention will modify local internal stress fields.
The proposed intervention is a 20–40% room-temperature thickness reduction followed by annealing below 400°C for approximately 30 minutes in inert gas or vacuum.
A sub-400°C anneal for approximately 30 minutes will relieve excessive residual stress without significant grain growth.
The increased density of grain boundaries will provide heterogeneous nucleation sites for the magnetostructural transition.
Induced texture and modified stress fields will reduce transition nucleation barriers.
Induced texture and modified stress fields will reduce pinning effects.
Lower nucleation barriers and reduced pinning will make the magnetostructural transition more gradual and spatially distributed.
The processed samples will show a broader magnetocaloric transition-temperature range than the baseline.
The processed samples will show reduced hysteresis during low-field magnetic-cooling cycles relative to the baseline.
Altered internal stress may slightly shift the transition temperature.
The predicted effects require annealing mild enough to avoid significant grain growth and secondary-phase formation.
The baseline material exhibits a sharp, hysteretic, first-order magnetostructural transition.

contradictions.description: The initial material is described as as-deposited, while the baseline is described as an 'as-deposited, arc-melted ingot or related standard processing route.' Arc melting and deposition are distinct processing states, so the actual control material is internally ambiguous.

The mechanism and falsification rule require correlation with altered internal stress, but the listed measurements do not directly measure residual or local stress; EBSD grain size and texture alone cannot establish that correlation.
